prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, ACA/Marketplace, Medicare, small‑business/employer group), whether you want an independent broker who shops multiple carriers, and where in the Kansas City metro you are (KC covers both Missouri and Kansas, which affects plan networks and regulators). If you tell me the type of plan and your ZIP code I can find and recommend a few highly rated local brokers.

To help you now, here’s how to find the best broker for your situation and what to ask:

Quick recommendations on where to look
- Prefer an independent broker or agency so you get multiple carrier options rather than someone tied to one insurer.  
- For Marketplace/ACA plans, search for certified assister/navigator programs through Healthcare.gov or your state exchange.  
- For Medicare, use your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) — they provide unbiased help.  
- Check online reviews (Google/Yelp), the Better Business Bureau, and state insurance department complaint records (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance and Kansas Insurance Department).

What to check about any broker
- Proper licensing: ask for their license number and verify it with the state insurance department.  
- Which carriers they represent (a full list) and whether they are independent.  
- Whether they charge a broker fee or are paid solely by commissions from insurers.  
- Experience with your specific needs (e.g., narrow network issues, chronic conditions, preferred doctors).  
- Will they help with enrollment, claim disputes, and annual plan reviews/changes?

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- “Do you work with multiple carriers or are you contracted with only one?”  
- “Which plans do you recommend for someone with [my needs: kids, chronic condition, preferred doctors, budget] and why?”  
- “Do you charge any fees? If so, how much and when?”  
- “How will you help if I have a claim problem later?”  
- “Can you provide references or client testimonials?”  
- “Are you licensed in Kansas and Missouri?” (if you need cross‑state coverage)

Red flags
- Refusal to show licensing info.  
- Pressure to pick a plan quickly or steer only to one insurer without explaining why.  
- Lack of willingness to help with future claims or appeals.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code, type of coverage (individual/family, Marketplace, Medicare, employer group), and a couple of priorities (price, provider continuity, prescription coverage). I’ll pull a short list of well‑rated local brokers/agencies and give tailored next steps.
